Event: `2830223d81be26f9f2b4a80ae615e5f2` · 2026-09-24T17:50:55Z

> PLAN v1, part 1/6: context, and section 1 (kernel-owned timer)
> 
> CONTEXT
> - Scheduling today is cooperative and PID round-robin: kmain's next_pid_to_run does SwitchTo, and threads run until they block or yield.
> - The hart timer is legacy IRQ 0. That covers timer_sbi.rs, irq.rs's timer::owns branches, platform/sbi/mod.rs TIMER_TIMEBASE/TIMER_SET_DEADLINE, and the timer-test program with its timer.toml case (also used in all-together.toml).
> - Redoubt timeouts exist as data. W_DEADLINE in each thread's IPC page is set by message::mark, but message::expire runs only at Redoubt syscalls (redoubt.rs:46) and in a polling idle loop (main.rs:147).
> - Budgets record weight and deadline (budget.rs), and nothing enforces either.
> - The model (model/src/sched.rs; kernel.rs tick/expire) already has a stride queue, logical time, timeouts and budget deadlines. But ties go to the lower budget id, tick re-picks at every event (so a timeout wake preempts), and a sleeper keeps a stale pass across an idle instant.
> 
> 1. TIMER
> - Backend is SBI TIME (sbi_rt::set_timer), not Sstc. It works under both prototyper builds and every SBI platform, including the planned FPGA softcores, and it is the code already in timer_sbi.rs. Sstc needs firmware to set menvcfg.STCE, and nothing tests that. RESOURCES permits Sstc by capability feature; I won't add an untested backend. One ecall per arming at a 10 ms slice is negligible.
> - New kernel/src/time.rs (portable), with timer_sbi.rs reduced to the backend:
>   - now_us() is unchanged.
>   - ticks_at(us) rounds up and saturates (FOREVER -> u64::MAX). The interrupt never fires before the µs deadline, so every interrupt finds something due and nothing livelocks.
>   - arm/disarm.
>   - Cached earliest-deadline hints: mark() lowers the thread hint and budget_create lowers the budget hint; expire recomputes both exactly. A stale hint is only ever early, costing one spurious interrupt, so nothing is missed (I13).
>   - Always armed while running: min(slice_end, earliest timeout, earliest budget deadline). Idle: min(deadlines), or disarm if there are none.
>   - Boot fails closed if the loader gave no Time timebase. Today it is max(1), which silently makes µs wrong.
> - Expiry: time::expire_due runs at every timer interrupt, at every kernel entry (legacy and Redoubt syscalls, external IRQs), and before a Redoubt call returns. This mirrors the model, which expires after every op. The hint makes the usual case one compare.
> - Due order is the model's: earliest deadline first; at an equal instant, timeouts before budget deadlines, then thread order or budget id. It matters. A caller in Reply whose timeout and whose server budget's deadline have both passed gets Timeout with the lend consumed if the timeout goes first, and Dead with the lend returned if the budget goes first. Today's expire takes the first match in walk order, so it is replaced.
> - rdtime: scounteren.TM is already set; K5 keeps and tests it. How user mode learns the frequency is question K5-q-timebase.
> - IRQ-0 removal:
>   - delete timer::IRQ, owns, mask and unmask, and the IRQ-0 dispatch in arch/riscv/irq.rs; SupervisorTimerInterrupt goes to time::on_interrupt only;
>   - platform_call timer ops are deleted and return UnhandledSyscall (K6 removes the plumbing), and the constants go from libs/abi/src/arch/riscv/mem.rs;
>   - delete tests/timer.toml and timer-test.rs, and drop timer-test with its irq=[0] grant from all-together.toml;
>   - fix the irq.rs doc comment;
>   - disable_all_irqs stops masking the timer;
>   - remove the polling idle branch, so idle is wfi with the timer armed.
>   - Loader and device.rs refusal of source 0 is unchanged (PLIC 0 doesn't exist).

Event: `e005b826285c5a246103b479df209f91` · 2026-09-24T17:51:08Z

> PLAN v1, part 2/6: section 2 (one stride queue over every runnable budget)
> 
> - State lives in the budget frame, as words after the current 16+MAX_LABELS: pass (u128, two words), tie (i64), queued (bool), and a round-robin cursor (pid, tid). Per-hart state is one KernelCell<Hart> in new kernel/src/sched.rs: running budget, slice start/end, switched_in. It is written so SMP can make it per hart.
> - Pure logic goes in a new crate libs/stride (redoubt-stride: no_std, zero deps, zero unsafe): step and wake arithmetic, ordering key, tie counters. It is host-tested and used by the kernel. The model keeps its own implementation; a dev-only differential test in libs/stride replays random sequences through both and requires identical picks and passes. The model gains no kernel dependency.
> - Arithmetic: step = min(runtime, 2^40) * STRIDE / weight, all in u64 (product < 2^60); pass: u128 += step.
>   - u128 is only used for add and compare, which are cheap on rv32 with no u128 mul/div. Starting at 0 at creation, it can't overflow in any lifetime.
>   - u128 is the model's type too, so there's no wrap logic.
>   - Everything is checked or saturating, so the overflow checks in checked builds can't panic (I14). Weight is never 0 (process_created already refuses weight-0 budgets).
> - Charging happens at EVERY deschedule. The one choke point is SystemServices::activate_process_thread, whenever the running (pid, tid) changes. That covers kmain dispatch, blocking (settle), yield, slice preemption, exit, and the legacy direct switches (borrowed-quantum send_message, IRQ callbacks). Each charge goes to the budget of the process that actually ran. PID 1 (kmain/idle) is charged to nobody. Runtime is counted in time ticks with a minimum of 1 per deschedule, so sub-µs bursts can't go free (K5-q-units).
> - Pick: kmain replaces next_pid_to_run with sched::pick.
>   - It walks the <=64 processes, collects budgets with a runnable thread, and takes the lowest (pass, tie, budget id).
>   - Inside that budget it takes the next runnable (pid, tid) after the budget's cursor: round-robin over all threads of all its processes (R12).
>   - Then SwitchTo, slice_end = now + SLICE, arm.
> - Wake: pass = max(own, current minimum).
>   - A wake is a budget going from 0 runnable threads to at least 1.
>   - Wakes are reconciled once per kernel entry, just before leaving the kernel, by comparing the runnable set with each budget's queued flag. That avoids hooking the dozen legacy ProcessState writers in services.rs; the model mirrors it once per op.
>   - Current minimum = the lowest pass of queued budgets, counting the running budget at its last-charged pass, floored by a monotone virtual-time floor that survives an empty queue (K5-q-minimum).
>   - Without the floor, a sleeper that wakes while nothing else is runnable keeps its old low pass, then starves everyone until it catches up. The model has this hole; its fairness generator always keeps a spinner running, so it never sees it.
> - Ties are deterministic and wake-first. tie is an i64 from two global counters:
>   - a wake takes front -= 1, so it ranks ahead of every queued equal;
>   - a requeue after deschedule (slice end, or a deadline re-pick with threads still runnable) takes back += 1, FIFO behind equals;
>   - wakes reconciled in the same entry go in ascending budget id (K5-q-ties).
>   Ties are the common case: every wake whose own pass is <= the minimum lands exactly on the minimum.
> - Preemption only at slice end or a deadline:
>   - A timer interrupt at slice_end charges the running budget, requeues it, and switches to kmain to re-pick. This is a forced yield through the existing activate_process_thread path with can_resume = true.
>   - A BUDGET deadline destroys the budget (section 4) and then re-picks.
>   - Timeout expiry and IRQ wakes only make threads runnable; the running thread keeps its slice (K5-q-preempt).
>   - A thread that blocks ends its own slice. Legacy direct switches continue the slice.

Event: `b709819964e5ed28c5196143f055699b` · 2026-09-24T17:51:19Z

> PLAN v1, part 3/6: sections 3 (timeouts) and 4 (budget deadlines)
> 
> 3. TIMEOUTS on call/send/receive
> - Representation is unchanged: W_DEADLINE in the thread IPC page = now + timeout, saturating; FOREVER never expires. mark() also lowers the time hint. settle() keeps its immediate Timeout for a deadline that has already passed (a poll). No new object and no allocation.
> - Armed in mark() via the hint, then time::rearm on the way out of the kernel.
> - Cancellation is implicit. wake, fail_wait, thread_ending and finish_served all set W_WAIT = None, and expiry ignores a deadline whose wait is None. A stale hint costs one spurious interrupt.
> - Races: one hart, SIE clear in the kernel, one lock, so kernel entry order decides everything. expire_due runs first at every entry, so a passed deadline beats any operation that enters later.
>   - Reply vs timeout: the reply's entry expires the caller first. Caller: Timeout, lend consumed, reply absent. Server's reply: discarded, mask 0 (IPC completion row 2). A reply before the deadline wins normally, and W_WAIT=None cancels the timeout.
>   - Queued call/send timeout: Timeout, lend/transfer returned (row 1). This is already fail_wait/unwind/give_buffer_back.
>   - Abandon: a Reply-waiter timing out abandons the call (R3): abandon(), then the server's one notice (I15), then pump. Already in fail_wait.
>   - Exit: a caller that dies first goes through thread_ending, so no timeout fires later. A server that dies first gives its caller Dead with the lend returned (row 3). Same-instant timeout and budget deadline use the fixed due order from section 1.
>   - Receive on an IRQ times out as today; R5 keeps the source masked until the next receive.
> - I13: every blocked thread with a finite deadline has its call completed (result committed, made runnable) by the first kernel entry at or after its deadline, and the timer guarantees there is such an entry. When it then runs is R12's business (K5-q-preempt).
> 
> 4. BUDGET DEADLINES
> - Refactor redoubt::budget_destroy into budget::destroy(ss, top, caller: Option<PID>). The syscall and the deadline path share it, so both use exactly today's R10 order:
>   (1) destroy_begin marks the subtree dying.
>   (2) Every process in it is killed, other processes first and the caller last (the deadline path has no caller).
>       - Notice: `killed` unless the creator is dying or the endpoint is dead; R1 applies; blame is always 0.
>       - Each thread goes through thread_ending (R4b). A pending call unwinds. A call held as server fails its caller with Dead and the lend returned. An abandoned lend is freed.
>   (3) process::budgets_dying frees process objects charged to the subtree, with no notice.
>   (4) message::budgets_dying:
>       - owned endpoints and devices are destroyed, and their waiters get Dead;
>       - queued messages sent through stamped handles fail with Dead;
>       - taken ones fail with Dead and are abandoned (R3), and the lend stays mapped in the server, charged to it, until its reply.
>   (5) destroy_marked sweeps handles everywhere, including unreceived messages, and returns limits to the parent (I10 once notices are received).
> - The deadline entry point is destroy_frame(top), which takes a frame, not a handle. Today pid is used only for handle lookup and the caller-last order.
> - expire_due destroys due budgets earliest (deadline, id) first, and skips descendants already destroyed with an ancestor.
> - A deadline already passed at budget_create is destroyed at that syscall's exit expiry; the returned handle is revoked at its next use. This matches the model, which expires after the op.
> - If the running process died, the trap returns to kmain (the Outcome::Resume / caller_doomed logic). The re-pick is as in section 2. root, system and users are FOREVER.

Event: `5e0bb8a049425d74659ccc5f5a532e87` · 2026-09-24T17:51:29Z

> PLAN v1, part 4/6: sections 5 (SMP and icache) and 6 (model)
> 
> 5. SMP
> - K5 stays single-hart for scheduling: one global queue under the existing big lock (KernelCell, which is a spinlock under `smp'), per RESOURCES' SMP stance.
> - Per-hart state is isolated in sched::Hart, and the SBI timer is per hart, so the post-M1 SMP work can split them.
> - The `smp' feature must build and smp-spike must pass on both widths. The spike runs before the scheduler and never arms the secondary's timer.
> - K5 claims nothing about multi-hart scheduling or IPC1 concurrent completion.
> - Icache (R2-followups item 5): the kernel has no fence.i.
>   - On one hart, a parent writes a child's code (process_map, or the stub via map_fixed), and nothing orders those stores before the child's first fetch.
>   - A physically tagged icache could also hold a previous owner's code for a recycled frame. That is a correctness hazard, not a privilege one: it runs in the new owner's context.
>   - Proposal: K5 owns only the single-hart piece. One fence.i right before a started process's first thread first runs (process_start), as its own small commit, adding 1 unsafe asm in arch/riscv. The multi-hart piece (fence on migration, or SBI remote fence.i) stays with the SMP work.
>   - QEMU can't observe it, so the evidence is code review. Question K5-q-icache.
> 
> 6. MODEL
> Files: model/src/sched.rs, kernel.rs (tick, expire, wake reconciliation), mutation.rs, check.rs, invariants.rs, tests/mutations.rs, README/VALIDATION counts.
> - Stride queue:
>   - add a tie key with front/back counters;
>   - reconcile wakes once per op, in ascending budget id;
>   - the minimum includes the running budget and the monotone floor (per the K5-q-minimum answer);
>   - a charge requeues at the back.
> - Running slice: the scheduler gains current: Option<(budget, tid, slice_start)>.
>   - tick runs `current' until the earliest of slice end, the op's end, or a BUDGET deadline.
>   - Timeouts and IRQs wake without a re-pick.
>   - A thread that blocks ends `current'. timer() stays slice end or next deadline.
> - expire already orders earliest first, timeouts ahead of budgets. Add a focused test that pins the Reply-timeout vs server-deadline outcome.
> - New properties:
>   (a) Ties: at a pick among equal passes, the budget woken latest wins.
>   (b) Preemption points: `current' changes only at slice end, block, exit or a budget deadline.
>   (c) Idle-gap banking: every budget sleeps at once, then a stale-pass sleeper wakes first; its share over the following interval stays within the bound.
>   (d) Sub-slice gaming: SLICE-eps run, 1 µs sleep, repeat; its share stays <= its weight plus the bound.
>   (e) The I13 check stays, plus a check that completion lands at the deadline tick.
> - New mutations, each with its catching property:
>   - R12TieQueuedFirst: (a) plus a focused example;
>   - R12PreemptOnWake: (b);
>   - R12NoFloorWhenIdle: (c);
>   - R12ShortRunsFree (runs under a slice charge 0): (d);
>   - R12RequeueAhead: (a);
>   - TimeoutIgnoredWhileOthersRun (expiry only when idle): I13;
>   - ExpireBudgetsFirst (equal-instant order): the focused outcome test.
>   - Existing R12PriorityById, R12IgnoreWeight, R12WakeBanksCredit and BudgetDeadlineIgnored must still be caught.
> - Evidence: the default suites, --test mutations (all detected), and one `million' run at the end, with counts in VALIDATION.md.
> - Differential: libs/stride dev tests replay random wake/block/charge/pick/deadline sequences through the stride crate (as the kernel wires it) and through redoubt_model::sched::Scheduler, and require identical picks and passes.

Event: `6e9f3f5b935501bf3c1b0a997b1514d2` · 2026-09-24T17:51:43Z

> PLAN v1, part 5/6: section 7 (tests)
> 
> Every boot case is kind=boot, arch rv64+rv32, a checked build.
> - Verdicts come from a trusted launcher/checker: the bundle's first program, which holds root/system/users and every device object.
> - Children are spawned with tests/programs/src/spawn.rs (a copy of the caller).
> - Spinners run the same counted loop, so a count ratio is a CPU-share ratio.
> - Tolerances are fixed in each case and justified from the model bound.
> 
> - sched-share (spinning budget bounded by weight): budgets 100/100/300 in `users', each spinning for T. Count ratios must be within tolerance of the weight ratios, and a victim's share must be >= w/W - tol.
> - sched-sleep-gaming (sleep/wake gaming): the gamer runs just under a slice, then sleeps 1 µs, repeating. Variants: long sleep then burst, and an idle-gap wake. Gamer share <= its weight share + tol; the equal-weight victim >= its share - tol.
> - sched-server-busy (system server busy on one user): a system-class server (weight 100 from `system') spins per request. User A floods it; users B and C spin. B and C must keep their shares - tol; A's flood buys only the server's weight.
> - sched-large-weight: a server at 1000 against N=8 users at 100, all spinning. Server share >= 1000/1800 - tol. The check is repeated inside the latency bench.
> - timeouts (I13, real timer; this closes IPC1's real-timers gate on the K5 side):
>   - sleep with the system otherwise IDLE (no syscalls anywhere, which proves the timer, not polling), and again with a spinner running;
>   - queued call (lend returned) and send time out;
>   - a taken call times out: lend consumed, the server gets one notice, and its reply is discarded;
>   - receive on an endpoint and on an IRQ;
>   - FOREVER, and near-u64::MAX saturation;
>   - 200 iterations of a reply racing the deadline at random offsets; each outcome must be one of the two legal rows;
>   - lateness reported;
>   - rdtime from U-mode: monotonic, rv32 hi/lo consistent, linear against time_now.
> - budget-deadline:
>   - Setup: a lease budget with a deadline, holding spinning children; a lend taken by a server outside it; a queued send; handles stamped with it held elsewhere; a child budget with a later deadline.
>   - Checks: killed notices with blame 0; the abandoned notice exactly once; Dead to the sender; handles 0 or BadHandle; parent usage restored (I10); a deadline already past at creation destroys the budget at once; FOREVER never fires; deadline-to-notice lateness reported.
>   - The running spinner covers preemption at a deadline.
> - sched-ties:
>   - New kernel feature sched-trace: a bounded in-kernel ring of wake/pick records {budget, weight, pass, tie, reason}, printed at system_reset.
>   - Sleepers at equal weight wake into a queue of spinners. The kernel prints a summary, and the case expects every equal-pass pick to choose the latest waker.
>   - The exact order is proven by the libs/stride host tests on the kernel's own code, by the differential and by the model mutations.
> - stride-host-tests (kind=host-tests, redoubt-stride). model-host-tests is unchanged.
> - The IRQ-0 `timer' case is deleted.
> - Every existing boot case is re-run on both widths, since preemption changes timing everywhere. The consoled flood case gets 1 cargo test plus the binary x20, no loops.
> 
> sched-latency, the named-workload bench:
> - Workload: N in {1,4,16} user budgets at weight 100 (INIT's user weight), each spinning; a driver at 1000 and a steward at 1000 (INIT), carved the way INIT carves them.
> - Driver: owns the QEMU virt goldfish RTC (its MMIO and IRQ device objects). K times: program the alarm at a random future RTC time T, receive on the IRQ handle, then read RTC time. Latency = t - T, on the RTC's own clock.
> - Steward stand-in: K times: create a lease under `users' and spawn a spinner in it; sleep until a random T (receive(none, timeout)); budget_destroy(lease); latency = time_now after destroy - T. The kernel-deadline lease path (deadline to killed notice) is also reported.
> - Recorded: weights, runnable-budget count and each budget's prior pass at every measured wake (from the sched-trace ring), and p50/p99/max for each N. The large-weight share check runs under the same load.
> - Target proposal:
>   - I post the table in this thread and propose a target, for example p99 <= X ms and max <= Y ms for N <= 16 on QEMU TCG, read off the data with margin.
>   - I expect about one slice (<= 10 ms plus overhead), since with 10x the weight the driver's own pass rarely exceeds the minimum.
>   - After reviewer acceptance, a final commit pins the target as the case's pass condition.
> - TCG timing follows host load, so I'd like a per-case QEMU `-icount shift=auto' option in the testbench.
> - The steward and drivers are stand-ins, since neither boots natively before R3/S2. Both points are asked in K5-q-bench.

> 4. Budget deadlines: the budget::destroy/destroy_frame refactor, the deadline path, and the budget-deadline case.
> 5. Stride scheduler:
>    - sched.rs with the budget-frame words; pick in main.rs; charging in services.rs activate_process_thread; slice-end preemption; deadline re-pick; legacy callback deferral.
>    - Cases: sched-share, sched-sleep-gaming, sched-server-busy, sched-large-weight.

> 
> RISKS
> - The inherited Xous scheduler state (ProcessState masks, SWITCHTO_CALLER asserts, borrowed-quantum switches, PREVIOUS_PAIR) now gets preempted at arbitrary user instructions, which cooperative scheduling never did. Mitigation: route everything through the existing yield path, and run checked builds of every case on both widths.
> - Legacy IRQ callbacks: only irq-attack and grant-attack claim IRQs, and neither depends on a callback running. The timer is no longer masked during a callback; slice-end preemption is deferred to finish_isr, while expiry still runs. K6 deletes callbacks.
> - Walks: each pick walks <= 64 processes; expiry uses the hint. The bench shows the cost.
> - QEMU TCG noise in the share and latency cases. Mitigation: tolerances from the model bound, medians over several windows, icount.
> - Timing-sensitive existing cases (ssh, consoled) may change.
> - Charging in ticks while the model uses µs is a constant scale, and the differential test runs in one unit.
> 
> QUESTIONS (separate threads)
> - K5-q-preempt: which events preempt; what I13's "returns" means
> - K5-q-minimum: floor/current-minimum definition
> - K5-q-ties: order among equal-pass wakers
> - K5-q-units: tick charging
> - K5-q-timebase: how users learn rdtime's frequency
> - K5-q-icache: fence.i scope
> - K5-q-bench: stand-ins, RTC, icount
>

Event: `0f9bea5461e28a5e8ba8afb5b29524bf` · 2026-09-24T17:53:14Z

> PLAN v1.1: K5-q-preempt answered (recommendations a and b). Changes to the plan:
> - The only preemption points are slice end and a BUDGET deadline. A timeout expiry or IRQ is a wake (pass = max(own, min), wake-first tie), and the running thread keeps its slice.
> - A budget deadline re-picks whichever budget's deadline fired: the running budget's partial slice is charged and it is requeued at the back (FIFO behind equals).
>   - New sub-case in budget-deadline: the deadline of a budget that is NOT running fires while a spinner runs. The sched-trace record must show the spinner charged a partial slice and a re-pick, and the destroyed budget's lateness is reported.
> - I13 reading, stated in the plan: the kernel commits the Timeout result and makes the thread runnable at the first kernel entry at or after the timeout. The always-armed timer bounds that entry by timer latency. When the thread then runs is R12's business. The K5 docs commit (commit 8) adds a one-line clarification to KERNEL-SPEC I13, so the model, kernel and tests share it.
> - Model (commit 1): tick no longer re-picks on a timeout wake. It re-picks only at slice end, block/exit or a budget deadline.
> - New mutation R12TimeoutWakePreempts: a timeout wake re-picks. > PLAN v1.2: K5-q-minimum answered (approved as defined). Changes to the plan:
> - Current minimum = the lowest pass among runnable budgets, including the running one at its last-charged pass. The floor is a monotone value that rises to that minimum whenever it changes and holds when the queue empties. Wake pass = max(own, floor).
> - Overflow (section 2): the floor has the same type as pass, u128, on rv32 and rv64.
>   - It is only compared and raised by max, never wrapped.
>   - It starts at 0 and never exceeds the largest pass. A pass can't overflow: each step is < 2^60 (runtime capped at 2^40 ticks x 2^20 / weight >= 1), and even 2^64 such steps stay far below 2^128.
>   - So no wrap-safe comparison is needed on either width. Passes and the floor use plain u128 ordering, which is also the model's type. All arithmetic is checked or saturating (I14).
> - New budgets: KERNEL-SPEC's budget table and R12 say nothing about an initial pass, and budget_create takes no scheduling argument. A budget starts at pass 0, and its first runnable thread is a wake, so it enters at max(0, floor) = floor. A new thread in an already-queued budget doesn't move the budget. Nothing in the spec contradicts this.
> - Docs commit: a one-line R12 clarification next to the I13 one.
> - Model: the same rule, plus mutation R12NoFloorWhenIdle, caught by the idle-gap property (c).
> - New boot case sched-idle-gap (rv64 and rv32, checked build, verdict from the launcher):
>   - A (weight 100) sleeps while B (weight 100) runs alone for about 2 s, so A's own pass stays far below B's.
>   - B blocks for a short gap (receive(none, timeout), about 5 ms). A's timeout is placed inside that gap, using absolute times the launcher computes from time_now, so A wakes while nothing else is runnable.
>   - Both then spin for a window W. Pass condition: B's work >= 1/2 - tol of the total. Without the floor, A would monopolise the CPU for about 2 s.
>   - Companion sub-case: a budget created and started during the gap must also enter at the floor, so its share over W is <= 1/2 + tol.
> - sched-idle-gap joins commit 5. The boot case count is now 10.

Event: `f64c487884a182dc387de6bcc5fd1fd1` · 2026-09-24T17:54:19Z

> PLAN v1.3: K5-q-ties answered (approved, with precisions). Changes to the plan:
> - RANK RULE among runnable budgets with an equal pass:
>   (1) every waker ranks ahead of every requeued budget;
>   (2) a wake in a later kernel entry (or model op) ranks ahead of one in an earlier entry (LIFO across entries);
>   (3) among wakes in the same entry, the lower budget id ranks ahead;
>   (4) requeues rank FIFO.
> - Implementation: the key is (pass, tie, id). Same-entry wakes are processed in DESCENDING budget id, each taking front -= 1, so the lowest id gets the frontmost key. A requeue takes back += 1.
> - Budget ids come from the kernel's next_object_id counter (budget.rs). They are never reused (I12), and no call takes an id, so no process can pick an id to win simultaneous ties. The only lever is creating a budget earlier to get an older, lower id. That affects only same-entry ties at an equal pass, and each run's charge advances the winner's pass, so the others still get their turn.
> - A wake is a budget going from zero runnable threads to at least one. Another thread of an already-queued budget becoming runnable doesn't move it.
> - Tie counters: front and back are i64s kept in u64 kernel words, the same on rv32 and rv64 (64-bit software arithmetic on rv32).
>   - Each moves by one per wake or requeue, so reaching 2^63 takes 2^63 scheduler events, centuries at one per ns.
>   - The arithmetic is saturating anyway, so no panic (I14). Saturation would only make those ties fall back to id order.
>   - Both reset to 0 whenever the queue is empty (no key is live then), which also keeps them small. The model does the same.
> - Mutations R12TieQueuedFirst and R12RequeueAhead are kept. The model differential and host tests pin the exact rank, including same-entry id order.
> - Boot case sched-ties (sched-trace kernel feature, rv64 and rv32). It exercises:
>   (i) a sleeper waking at the floor ties with the queued spinner, and the sleeper runs first;
>   (ii) two sleepers with timeouts at the same instant wake in one kernel entry at an equal pass: lower id first, then higher, both ahead of the spinner;
>   (iii) a slice-end requeue goes behind equals.
>   The kernel prints a summary of every equal-pass pick with its rank reason; the case expects all three patterns and forbids any violation line.
> - One KERNEL-SPEC docs commit carries all three clarifications: I13, current minimum/floor, and ties/rank.

> PLAN v1.4: K5-q-units answered (approved, plus an exact remainder). Changes to the plan:
> - Charging is in timebase ticks, with a minimum of 1 per deschedule and runtime capped at 2^40 ticks. Timeouts and deadlines stay in µs per the ABI.
> - EXACT REMAINDER (overflow section): each budget frame gains a word rem.
>   - At each charge: t = rem + ticks x STRIDE; step = t / weight; rem = t % weight; pass (u128) += step.
>   - Bounds: ticks x STRIDE <= 2^40 x 2^20 = 2^60, and rem < weight <= 2^32 - 1, so t < 2^61 fits u64 on rv32 and rv64. No saturation is needed on this path; it is checked arithmetic that can't fail.
>   - Charging is then exact over any sequence and never free for any weight. There is no step >= 1 floor, which would overcharge large weights.
>   - rem is set to 0 only at budget creation. A wake doesn't clear it: raising the pass to the floor doesn't erase fractional debt.
>   - Today's weights are carved from ROOT_WEIGHT = 1000 (budget.rs), so none can currently exceed 2^20. But the ABI field is a u32, and without the carry even small weights lose up to one unit per deschedule. So the remainder is unconditional.
> - Model: stays in µs, since the differential against libs/stride runs in one unit, and carries the same rem.
>   - Its batched charge_slices stays exact: carrying the remainder across n charges equals one charge of the total, so batching is still identical to slice-by-slice.
>   - New mutation R12DropRemainder (step = floor, remainder discarded), caught by an extension of the gaming property (d): a weight-2^24 budget running 1 µs bursts against an equal-weight spinner must stay within its share. Under the mutation its pass never advances.
>   - R12ShortRunsFree stays for sub-slice runs charged 0. The mutation count is now 9.
> - The KERNEL-SPEC clarification commit's R12 line gains: runtime is charged in ticks with an exact per-budget remainder.
> - The libs/stride host tests add exhaustive small-weight checks and random large-weight checks: the sum of steps over any split of a runtime equals the step of the total, given the carried remainder.

Event: `791d69acfea2339b8d83c5143845b806` · 2026-09-24T17:56:08Z

> PLAN v1.6: K5-q-icache answered (K5 owns the single-hart piece). I checked every path. Commit 7 now fences at X installation, not only at process_start.
> 
> Paths to executable bytes:
> - Lends and transfers are mapped R|W only (arch/riscv/mem.rs map_into), so they are never X in the receiver. A transferred page becomes X only through the receiver's own set_flags. A borrowed page can't be set_flags'd (not the caller's own mapping).
> - map_device and dma_alloc map R|W.
> - process_map is refused once the child has started (process.rs:366, NotPermitted). The kernel never installs X into a running process except at that process's own request: map_anon/map_fixed with X, or set_flags adding X.
> - W^X (R11): a page's contents can change only while it isn't X. So every write-then-fetch path, whoever wrote the bytes, passes through a kernel call that installs X: process_map, map_anon, map_fixed or set_flags. The writer can be the parent, the owner, the kernel's zeroing, or DMA into a dma_alloc page.
> 
> Decision: the kernel fences, rather than making it the process's job.
> - arch::riscv::mem::sync_icache() is one fence.i, the only new unsafe asm.
> - It runs after any successful call that installs or adds X (process_map, map_anon, map_fixed, set_flags), before the return to user mode, and once at boot before the first user dispatch, which covers loader-written images.
> - On one hart this orders every earlier store before any fetch through the new mapping, so no process needs its own fence.i for memory it got through syscalls. U-mode fence.i stays legal and harmless (the stub keeps its own).
> 
> Recycled frames: a stale, physically tagged line can only be fetched through an X mapping, and every X installation is followed by the kernel's fence.i on this hart. That instruction synchronises the hart's instruction stream with all earlier stores, including the kernel's zeroing of the recycled frame.
> - Under a "process's responsibility" rule, a hostile new owner could map RX, skip the fence, and execute a victim's stale code, which is a cross-process confidentiality leak. That's why the fence belongs in the kernel.
> 
> Multi-hart (not K5): X installation on one hart doesn't fence the others, and migration needs a fence on the destination hart (or SBI remote fence.i). It stays with post-M1 SMP (PLAN, SMP) and is noted in QA R2-followups item 5.
> 
> Commit 7 is its own small commit, with the unsafe ratchet updated honestly (+1). The argument above goes in the commit message for the red team. The evidence is code review only; QEMU can't observe it.

> - A new budget starts at pass 0 and so enters at the floor on its first wake; the spec is silent on an initial pass (q-minimum).

> PLAN v2: every K5-plan-review finding, with its disposition. This is on top of v1.1 plus the orchestrator's P1-2 rule. Still PLAN ONLY. The full consistent text, which supersedes v1 where they differ, is at ~/.claude/plans/wash-inbox-1-message-iterative-comet.md.
> 
> P1-1 FREE CPU ON EXIT PATHS: ACCEPTED; accounting moves to the trap boundary.
> - There are exactly two sret sites, _redoubt_resume_context (via arch::syscall::resume) and _redoubt_syscall_return_result (via irq.rs return_registers), and one trap entry, trap_handler.
> - EXIT HOOK (resume/return_registers, when returning to U): if the target's budget differs from Hart.running, deschedule the old budget (fold, requeue with back += 1) and set running. Then record user_since and user_budget as a (frame, id) BudgetRef, and rearm.
> - ENTRY HOOK (first thing in trap_handler when SPP=User, before anything reads the process): pending += now - user_since, for user_budget.
> - No U-mode instruction runs outside a return/entry pair, so thread_exit (destroy_thread -> switch_to_thread), process_exit, faults, kills (terminate_process -> switch_to_thread) and callback switches can't skip it.
> - Passes still change only at a FOLD: a budget change at exit, a kmain pick, a slice-end or deadline preemption, or a destroy. So R12's "at every deschedule" holds literally, and the exact remainder makes the split charges equal the total.
> - New boot case sched-exit-churn: thread churn plus process exit and fault churn; victim share >= 1/2 - tol, asserted.
> - New model mutation R12ExitRunsFree (exit/fault/kill of `current' drops its partial run), caught by the new exit-churn fairness property (f).
> 
> P1-2 BUDGET CHURN: ORCHESTRATOR RULE R6, a pass inherited through the tree, to be confirmed by the owner.
> - Create: child pass = max(floor, PARENT budget pass), rem = 0.
> - Destroy (syscall, deadline or revocation): bottom-up in R10 order, before destroy_marked, fold the dying budget's pending time (including a running one), then parent.pass = max(parent, child).
> - Proof it closes the loop: a pass is a virtual-time position, the point up to which a budget has been served.
>   - Loop create C, run, destroy: C starts at >= P.pass. When destroyed it leaves P.pass >= C's final pass = start + (run x STRIDE)/w_C. The next child starts there.
>   - So the sequence of children is charged exactly like one continuous budget of weight w_C whose pass carries over, and gains nothing over running in the parent.
>   - Concurrent siblings each run fairly at their own weights. The parent takes max(c_i), so a successor starts no earlier than any sibling's service point.
>   - max is right and a sum would double-count: the siblings consumed in parallel while the floor advanced.
>   - Carving is unaffected: weight returns to the parent at destroy (R7), and pass is a position, not an amount, so nothing is counted twice.
>   - Loss: rem < w_C at destroy, i.e. under 1 pass unit per destroyed budget, and every creation is itself a charged syscall.
> - Parking variant (a fresh intermediate M per cycle): each M holds >= 1 carved weight until it is destroyed, and destroying it pushes its debt up. So parked free entries are bounded by the attacker budget's weight limit, and any destroy repays them.
> - Cross-subtree residual: a child's pass is <= floor + one step (a runnable budget only runs at the minimum), so debt parked on a shared parent (users/system) delays later siblings by at most one slice at the child's weight. Only init and the steward create there, at manifest weights >= 100. This is stated.
> - New boot case sched-budget-churn: weight-1 child create/run-one-slice/destroy loop, plus the parking variant. Asserted: victim >= 1/2 - tol, attacker subtree <= 1/2 + tol.
> - New model mutations R12DestroyDropsDebt and R12CreateAtFloorOnly, both caught by the churn property (g), which includes parking.
> - The R12/R7 clarification goes in the docs commit.
> 
> P1-3 EXPIRY KILLS STATE THE TRAP CAPTURED: ACCEPTED; per-entry protocol, with no expect() on a killable pid.
> - kmain (PID 1) SwitchTo entry: NO expiry. kmain runs expire_due -> reconcile -> fold -> pick -> SwitchTo with no entry in between. A failed SwitchTo re-picks and no longer panics.
> - Redoubt and legacy ecalls from U: entry hook -> expire_due -> re-read current; if the caller's (pid, tid) is gone, skip the call and resume current; otherwise dispatch with the re-read pid.
> - External IRQ from U: re-read after expiry, BEFORE PREVIOUS_PAIR is recorded.
> - Timer from U: after expiry, if current died -> kmain; the slice check otherwise.
> - Timer or IRQ from S (idle): expiry, then resume PID 1.
> - EXIT_THREAD, RETURN_FROM_ISR, RETURN_FROM_EXCEPTION_HANDLER and faults: after expiry, if the thread died, skip thread_exit/faulted/fault handling and resume current.
> - expire_due runs once per entry. A past-deadline budget_create is destroyed at the next entry.
> 
> P2-1 LEGACY CALLBACKS: ACCEPTED as a guard plus a stated residual.
> - While PREVIOUS_PAIR is set, timeouts still expire (they only wake), but budget-deadline destruction and slice-end preemption are deferred to just after finish_isr's resume, through the normal path.
> - finish_isr with a dead previous pair resumes current instead of expect().
> - The preempt path activates PID 1 directly with SWITCHTO_CALLER reset: no do_yield, no expect.
> - Residual until K6: a callback that never returns keeps the CPU. Only manifest-granted IRQs can be claimed (grants::may_claim_irq; interrupt_claim refuses device-object IRQs), and after K5 the only claimants are the irq-attack/grant-attack refusal tests. The v1 claim that "a callback can't hold off slice ends" is withdrawn.
> 
> P2-2 THE DEADLINE PATH ISN'T CALLER-LESS: ACCEPTED.
> - If the interrupted current process is in the doomed subtree, it is the caller, killed last via process::killed; the path returns to kmain. kill_process never targets current.
> - Hart.running is a (frame, id) BudgetRef with a liveness check. Pending time is folded and propagated (R6), and dying budgets are purged from the queued set and Hart.running, all before destroy_marked frees frames. No scheduling word is written into a freed or reused frame.
> 
> P2-3 KERNEL WORK BILLED TO THE VICTIM: ACCEPTED, with a billing rule.
> - U-mode time goes to the budget that ran it.
> - Syscall time (entry to exit) goes to the caller's budget, folded during destroy if the call kills that budget.
> - Expiry work, wherever it runs and including the one shared walk, goes to the budget of the FIRST due item in due order: a timeout's thread budget, or a deadline's dying budget.
> - Slice-end overhead goes to the running budget (constant per slice). IRQ handling goes to the IRQ device's owner budget.
> - The kernel keeps only: spurious interrupts from stale hints (<= 1 per cancelled deadline, and each cancel follows a charged syscall), kmain's O(64) pick, and idle.
> - Bound: at most O(1) uncharged kernel work per charged syscall, and nothing is billed to a victim.
> - New boot case sched-timer-flood: the attacker maxes out threads and processes with 1 µs-staggered sleepers, with a lease-deadline variant; victim >= 1/2 - tol, asserted.
>

>   (2) return its weight to the parent, folding the parent first;
>   (3) W = (child.pass - f)+ x w_child + child.rem, where f is the floor, w_child the child's stride weight and w_parent the parent's stride weight AFTER the return;
>   (4) candidate = (f + W / w_parent, W % w_parent);
>   (5) the parent's (pass, rem) takes the candidate if it is larger in (pass, rem) order.

> - Entry stays max(floor, parent.pass), after folding a running parent's pending time (N8): inheriting a wait needs no scaling, but moving work does.

>   - every run by a destroyed descendant ends up charged to its ancestor at the ancestor's stride weight, exactly as if the ancestor ran it;
>   - free weights sum to at most root's, so a subtree's long-run share is at most its free-weight share;
>   - waits are inherited unscaled and max never lowers an ancestor, so create/destroy without a run gains nothing;
>   - residual per destroy: a remainder under 1 unit, plus the w_child/w_parent conversion of the inherited entry wait, which is at most one ancestor step because a child runs only at the minimum;
>   - asserted by model property (g) and sched-budget-churn, including the parking variant.

> - The single shared walk is billed to the kernel.
> - syscall_since starts after entry expiry, so a caller is never billed for others' expiries.
> 
> N4 BOUND MISSTATED: ACCEPTED; indexed and restated.
> - Budgets with finite deadlines go on an intrusive list threaded through their frames (link on create, unlink on destroy). The deadline-hint walk is O(D), D = live finite-deadline budgets, each paid for with a budget page. It never scans 0..high_frame.
> - True bound: at most ONE uncharged walk of O(T + D) per kernel entry, T <= 64 x 31 thread IPC pages. A walk runs only when the hint is due, and a hint is early only after a cancel or destroy, each of which follows a charged syscall. So uncharged work is <= one O(T + D) walk per charged syscall, plus one per real due event, plus kmain's O(64) pick per deschedule.
